engagement.name: Project Helios - Annual Red Team Engagement
engagement.scope: Payment portal, customer API gateway, corporate VPN, cloud identity stack

findings.title: SQL Injection in customer export endpoint
findings.description: The /api/export endpoint concatenates user-supplied date parameters directly into a SQL query. A crafted payload allowed full database extraction of PII records.
findings.technical_impact: Severity of PII extraction and data integrity destruction in the payments database.
findings.business_impact: Regulatory exposure under GDPR and PCI DSS; potential brand and revenue impact.
findings.remediation: Migrate all queries to parameterized statements; apply strict allow-list validation on all date inputs; add WAF rules and run DAST in CI.
findings.evidence: Boolean-based blind injection returned 200 with row count 1 when payload IF(1=1,...)

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) on invoice endpoint
findings.description: Invoice detail endpoint trusts the invoice_id path parameter without ownership verification, enabling enumeration of other customers' invoices.
findings.technical_impact: Unauthorized disclosure of financial records for any account.
findings.business_impact: Customer data leakage; reputational and legal risk.
findings.remediation: Enforce ownership-based authorization checks on every object reference; consider randomized identifiers and signed references.
findings.evidence: Sequential ID enumeration returned invoices for 40+ unrelated accounts without authentication errors.

findings.title: SSRF via PDF generator allows internal network scanning
findings.description: The invoice PDF generator fetches arbitrary user-controlled URLs, permitting access to the cloud metadata service and internal microservices.
findings.technical_impact: Internal network reconnaissance and access to cloud metadata (IMDS) with temporary credentials.
findings.business_impact: Lateral movement enabler; potential compromise of internal services and secrets.
findings.remediation: Restrict outbound traffic from generator service, block link-local/metadata ranges, allow-list trusted hosts, and adopt URL schema validation.
findings.evidence: Request to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ returned IAM role name for the service account.

findings.title: Weak TLS cipher suites on corporate VPN
findings.description: VPN concentrator accepts TLS 1.0/1.1 and export-grade cipher suites. Man-in-the-middle decryption of management plane traffic is feasible.
findings.technical_impact: Captured VPN handshakes can be downgraded/decrypted, exposing session material.
findings.business_impact: Credential and session exposure for remote workforce.
findings.remediation: Disable TLS < 1.2, remove export/weak cipher suites (e.g., CBC, RC4, 3DES), enforce certificate pinning policies.
findings.evidence: TLS scan reported 14 insecure cipher suites including TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.

findings.title: Privileged access via default admin token in developer console
findings.description: Cloud identity stack ships a documented default service-account token that grants full admin on the developer console when not rotated.
findings.technical_impact: Full administrative control of identity platform datasets and delegated authentication flows.
findings.business_impact: Complete compromise of identity and access management; supply-chain risk to all downstream applications.
findings.remediation: Rotate tokens, disable default credentials, enforce MFA + conditional access on the console, and review privileged role assignments.
findings.evidence: Documented default token accepted and issued cloud-admin scoped session.

findings.title: Outdated third-party library with known RCE (Apache Log4j core)
findings.description: Payment scheduler bundles Log4j-core 2.14.1, affected by Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) family. Chained with a JNDI-capable sink it permits remote code execution.
findings.technical_impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on the scheduler host.
findings.business_impact: Ransomware and data-exfiltration staging point on payment path.
findings.remediation: Upgrade Log4j to >= 2.17.1 or 3.x; add SCA scanning to CI; inventory all Java runtimes; verify no JNDI sinks remain.
findings.evidence: Chained ${jndi:ldap://...} payload triggered outbound LDAP callback from scheduler host.

findings.title: Security events not logged for failed administrative logins
findings.description: Admin console silently drops failed authentication attempts from audit logs; no SIEM alerting exists for brute-force or account lockout bypass.
findings.technical_impact: Brute-force and credential-stuffing campaigns against admin accounts are invisible to security teams.
findings.business_impact: Delayed detection of account takeover; compliance gaps in audit proof.
findings.remediation: Emit structured audit events for all auth failures, ship them to SIEM, tune alert rules, and test detection scenarios.
findings.evidence: 1,200 failed admin logins over 72h produced zero alerts and zero events in SIEM search.

findings.title: Unused services exposed on public firewall rules
findings.description: Public IP range exposes FTP (21), SNMP (161) and a legacy admin panel; firewall rules contradict documented architecture and allow probes of internal services.
findings.technical_impact: Expanded attack surface; SNMP default community strings readable.
findings.business_impact: Unauthorized reconnaissance and abuse of legacy features.
findings.remediation: Apply least functionality: close 21/161, remove admin panel from the internet, and centralize change reviews for firewall rules.
findings.evidence: External scan enumerated FTP banner of internal build server (reveals hostname).

findings.title: Missing rate limiting on password reset allows MFA bypass
findings.description: Password reset endpoint issues a 6-digit code without rate limiting or lockout; brute-forcing the code in-band bypasses the MFA step.
findings.technical_impact: Account takeover of any user with a single reset code brute force.
findings.business_impact: Widespread account compromise; regulatory notification obligations.
findings.remediation: Rate limit reset attempts, use short-lived high-entropy tokens, bind reset to session, require re-authentication for critical actions, and monitor anomalous reset flows.
findings.evidence: 6-digit code brute-forced within 2 hours using distributed request pattern without trigger of WAF or SIEM rules.
